QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_1

question.text: Mr. Arvind Mehta, CIO of Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF), is drafting the risk-policy preamble and wants to cite the foundational contribution of Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT). Which of the following BEST describes the specific contribution of Harry Markowitz's 1952 'Portfolio Selection' article?

answer.text: It introduced beta as the sole measure of a security's risk and priced assets accordingly.
It introduced the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) linking expected return to systematic risk.
It proved that investors must borrow at the risk-free rate to maximise risk-adjusted returns.
It mathematically quantified the benefit of diversification by using covariance/correlation and showed that the variance of returns is a meaningful measure of portfolio risk.

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter explicitly credits Harry Markowitz's 1952 'Portfolio Selection' (published in the Journal of Finance) with (i) quantifying diversification through covariance/correlation and (ii) showing variance of the rate of return is a meaningful measure of portfolio risk. Markowitz received the 1990 Nobel Prize for this work. The Trap: Option A describes CAPM's beta framework (Sharpe/Lintner/Treynor/Mossin 1960s), not MPT. Option B is CAPM which builds on MPT but came later. Option C refers to the Capital Market Line borrowing-lending insight, again post-MPT. Note: Page 50 of the workbook contains the Markowitz/MPT contribution; page 57 supports the variance-covariance matrix context.
